lines.text: Three hundred and fifty-two overtakes. Thirty-five changes of lead.
And somehow, Max Verstappen still came out on top in Las Vegas.
Verstappen wins in Vegas!
Mercedes, three laps from glory.
Piastri, seventeenth to the podium!
And Ferrari? Leclerc spins Hamilton. Again.
Max Verstappen won it, and led forty-five of the fifty laps.
But the top five? Covered by three seconds at the flag!
Lando Norris second, six tenths back, and Oscar Piastri third.
Then Kimi Antonelli and Pierre Gasly, both inside three seconds of the winner.
That's win number seventy-five for Verstappen, and his third in Las Vegas.
His fourth win this year... and all four came in the last six Grands Prix.
And pole? Antonelli was quickest in qualifying, but a new engine cost him five places, so Verstappen inherited it.
Pix! He won the first one back, in twenty twenty-three, the first F1 race in Vegas since nineteen eighty-two!
lines.note: Matches anecdotes.json supported_wording; Wikipedia confirms 2023 race was first F1 race in Las Vegas since 1982 and Verstappen won.

lines.text: And Red Bull's boss Laurent Mekies? He says Max is "from a different planet."
lines.note: Mekies quote "from a different planet" is 4 words, verbatim in F1.com article; attributed.

lines.text: Fresh off the teams' title, they were in the fight for the win.
lines.note: Mercedes confirmed constructors champions the week before (Mercedes-AMG F1 site).

lines.text: Three laps to go: George Russell locks up and slides into the barrier at Turn Five.
He kept going, and finished ninth. No regrets about attacking, he says.
Then, on the penultimate lap, Antonelli lifts, gets back on the throttle... and his battery deployment takes the hit.
Both McLarens go past. Fourth.
Toto Wolff reckons Antonelli would have just saved it over the line to win.
Oscar Piastri started SEVENTEENTH, after a power unit penalty...
...and finished THIRD! Fourteen places! The biggest comeback of his career!
His first podium since Miami in May, too.
And it takes me back... Kimi Raikkonen, Suzuka, two thousand and five. Won it from seventeenth!
lines.note: Source: P17 to victory, Suzuka, 2005 Japanese GP.

lines.text: And Lando Norris dropped as far back as eleventh... and still finished second!
That's his fifth top-five finish in a row.
The fight for third in the teams' championship? Red Bull's lead is down to NINE points, with two rounds left!
At Turn Seven, Charles Leclerc knocked Lewis Hamilton into a spin.
Hamilton lost four places, and recovered to seventh.
Leclerc got a ten-second penalty, and finished tenth.
Oh, and both Ferraris went out in Q2.
Fred Vasseur says he'll talk to the drivers the next day.
Haas have confirmed him for Qatar and Abu Dhabi, ahead of his full-time debut next year.
In Vegas, Checo Pérez hit the back of his Haas approaching Turn Fourteen, and retired.
The stewards put it wholly on Pérez: his ten-second penalty became a five-place grid drop for Qatar.
Camara? Sixteenth.
Camara leads Formula Two by seven points over Nikola Tsolov.
And by racing in F1 instead, The Race says he sacrifices his shot at that title.
Alex Dunne is third, eleven points behind Tsolov.
Walking away from a title you're leading? That takes some nerve.
lines.note: Hidden claim that Camara currently leads F2; supported by The Race (leads by 7).

lines.text: Three hundred and fifty-two, Pix! By F1's own figures!
That's almost one for every day of the year.
lines.note: F1.com: almost one for every day of the year (352).

lines.text: The first Vegas race, back in twenty twenty-three? A hundred and eighty-one moves.
lines.note: Mercedes-AMG preview: 181 moves across the grid in 2023.

lines.text: And lead changes? Monza, nineteen sixty-five, had around forty!
lines.note: Wikipedia: 42 lead changes, most ever; script says around forty, within supported wording.

lines.text: So thirty-five is close. But Monza keeps the crown.
lines.note: Hidden claim that Monza 1965 holds the record: Wikipedia says 42 lead changes, the most ever in an F1 race; 35 is fewer. Supported.

lines.text: But the drivers? Split.
Verstappen won it, and still criticised the overtaking frenzy.
Checo Pérez called it very artificial. Carlos Sainz and Lewis Hamilton enjoyed it.
lines.note: Perez said "very artificial" (sarcastic summary, The Race); Sainz and Hamilton enjoyed it.

lines.text: Pierre Gasly finished fifth, under three seconds from the win. His best result of the season.
lines.note: Source: Gasly 5th, best result of the season (The Race).

lines.text: With his power turned down for forty-five of the fifty laps!
An overheating issue. He says he was losing over a second a lap.
And Franco Colapinto? Sixth, matching his best Grand Prix result.
Colton Herta won't race the last two rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
Roman Bilinski takes his Hitech seat, Sebastian Montoya moves from Prema to DAMS, and Nicola Lacorte joins Prema.
Isack Hadjar started fourth, lost his front wing right after the restart, and a penalty dropped him to fifteenth.
Arvid Lindblad started a career-best fifth, then spun behind the Safety Car.
Cadillac keep Valtteri Bottas for twenty twenty-seven, alongside Checo Pérez.
Josef Newgarden signs a multiyear extension with Team Penske.
And OpenAI will sponsor Alex Palou's car for the whole of twenty twenty-seven.
Next up: Qatar, round twenty-two of twenty-three.
Nine points between Red Bull and McLaren, and two races to go!
